completeness: Migration audience or required configuration is absent or wrong.
A major required action, preserved behavior or platform evidence limitation is missing or incorrect.
All essential migration and evidence boundaries are present; only a minor supporting detail or citation needs correction.
Covers affected/unaffected users, old-path resolution, replacement, pre-restart check, rejected forms, unchanged data/behavior and exact observed/not-run platform scope.
clarity: Reader cannot determine whether or how the notice applies.
Affected users, steps or testing caveats are scattered or conflated and require source reconstruction.
Applicability and ordered action are clear, with a small wording or evidence-placement issue.
Maintainers can quickly distinguish who acts, what to change, what stays intact and which test evidence is absent; examples are clearly optional.
usefulness: Notice would lead to incorrect migration, data loss or unsupported rollout confidence.
A maintainer must substantially rewrite the notice or inspect sources to identify the necessary safe steps.
Maintainers can plan the correct change and check, with a minor clarification needed.

A scheduled-job maintainer can decide whether action is required, identify the correct existing directory, change only the relevant key and plan validation while seeing platform evidence limits; manual users can see no action is required.

grading: Hard gates and reader dimensions are separate. Score each dimension independently, including baseline failures. A score never overrides a failed or not_run hard gate.
